final_claim.narrative: Using a candidate change point c = 41000 (half-windows [36000,41000] and [41001,46000]) several group members show a complete turnover of partners: 384 had many partners before and zero after (steps 01–02); 716 and 946 had large, non-overlapping partner sets before and only a couple/new partners after (steps 03–06); 948 was inactive before and had many partners after (steps 07–08). The sampled before/after contact sets are essentially disjoint (Jaccard ~0, dissimilarity ~1) at this candidate change point, exceeding the 0.6 threshold for an abrupt regime switch. The mixed patterns of activity (some nodes dropping to zero, others becoming active) argue against a simple global inactivity confound and support a partner-regime change. Confidence is moderate because the direct neighbor queries cover a subset of the group members but the observed turnover among the queried nodes is strong and temporally concentrated.
